content:
- Overweight recent spikes in sentiment when forecasting short-term (30d) moves; model tends to overreact and overshoot after positive sentiment spikes.
- Underweight negative sentiment in early periods; model often fails to adjust downward when sentiment is consistently negative, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after sharp upward moves, forecasts tend to overcorrect downward, missing the true continuation or reversal.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; model often lags 1–2 days behind sentiment-driven price shifts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate upside; when sentiment is negative, it underestimates downside — create asymmetric correction based on sentiment polarity.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend without sentiment confirmation; if sentiment turns negative after a spike, reduce forecast momentum by 15–20%.
- For 30d forecasts, apply a 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative values.
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal from negative to positive, model often fails to adjust forecast mid-horizon — apply a 10–15% upward correction after 5–7 days of positive sentiment.
